checked: Intent and profile type restated: one stored per-project record replaces Bun/TS assumptions; fields are coherent individually.
Init flow restated: notice at load, Architect session proposes, proves each command once, reports map numbers, owner confirms then stored; consistent with bullets under it.
Readers table rows for guidance, auto-fix, tool lookup and Bun hang guard restate cleanly against the type.
Build order steps 1-5 are sequenced consistently with the reader table, except for the items in findings.

findings.what: With no profile the plan says work runs 'as today', yet step 5 replaces deriveSourceDefinition and the Fallow config demand with profile-driven reads. My restatement: either an absent profile keeps a built-in default source filter and Fallow gate, or those readers need a profile and the no-profile path changes.
findings.failureScenario: One builder removes deriveSourceDefinition so a project without a profile gets no map or audit; another keeps a hard-coded fallback, leaving the special-casing the plan says should not remain.
evidence: "Not a gate: with no profile, work runs with the Architect's own commands as today."
findings.suggestion: State what each reader does when the profile is absent (map, audit, Fallow gate, recheck).

findings.what: The plan says LAZERS 'becomes a profile with Bun commands' but not how: seeded by migration, or the init notice and Architect setup run on LAZERS itself. The Bun test hang guard also 'becomes part of a Bun profile's commands' without saying where the guard text lives.
findings.failureScenario: Existing projects, including LAZERS, silently lose the hang guard and Fallow gate until someone runs setup; or a builder hard-codes a seed that contradicts the Architect-proves-it flow.
evidence: "LAZERS itself becomes a profile with Bun commands; nothing special stays in the code."
"Bun test hang guard | becomes part of a Bun profile's commands"
findings.suggestion: Say whether existing projects are seeded or must go through init, and what happens between deploy and setup.

findings.what: Several fields do not say how they work. `fix.files` is undefined (what is matched, per command?). `source.exports` is one string but the text says it names a method 'per language'. `verify` entries carry no toolchain link although two toolchains share one profile. The 'lockfile' used by the recheck is read from nowhere in the type.
findings.failureScenario: Builders implement fix.files as a staged-file filter, a glob or a run-once flag; exports as a single scanner name or a language map; the recheck guesses lockfiles by name, defeating 'one definition'.
evidence: "exports?: string // how exported names are found, per language"
findings.suggestion: Define fix.files, make exports a language-keyed map or say it is one scanner, and say how lockfiles are determined (derived from toolchains or listed in profile).

findings.what: 'Dismiss' appears only in the last bullet; the flow diagram, store and Settings group have no dismissed state, and 'records the result' of each command has no field in ProjectProfile.
findings.failureScenario: A builder either has no way to dismiss (notice nags forever) or invents a store for dismissal and for run results with no home in the profile.
evidence: "The notice stays until the owner sets up or dismisses it."
"runs each command once and records the result"
findings.suggestion: Name where dismissal and per-command proof results are stored.

findings.what: The closing paragraph makes steps 2 and 4 depend on a split of src/runner/runtime.ts whose 'effect reconciliation' and 'verification candidate' modules are named nowhere else in design/; no plan for the split was found (grep of design/ for 'runtime-split' and 'verification modules' returned only this file).
findings.failureScenario: The profile builders either do the split themselves, widening scope, or start step 2 against the old monolith and conflict with the parallel split.
evidence: "The split of `src/runner/runtime.ts` moves the verification modules first (check activities, verification candidate, effect reconciliation)"
findings.suggestion: Link the split plan or say whether it is a prerequisite or part of this work.

findings.what: `audit` is one flag per project and `source` one filter, but a project with two toolchains (the plan's own example) may have Fallow-readable and unreadable parts. It is unclear whether 'fallow' then applies to the whole tree or only to files matching source.include.
findings.failureScenario: A TypeScript plus Rust project gets Fallow run over, or refused on, the whole tree depending on the builder's reading.
evidence: "audit: \"fallow\" | \"off\" // Fallow only where it can read the code"
"A project with two toolchains carries both in one profile."
findings.suggestion: State that Fallow reads only files matching source.include, or that audit applies per project.

questions.question: Should existing projects, including LAZERS, be seeded with a profile on upgrade, or all go through the init notice?
questions.why: Seeding needs a migration and a Bun default; init-only means no hang guard or Fallow gate until setup.
options: Seed any project that has Bun tooling

questions.question: With no profile, do the map, audit and recheck keep today's built-in behavior?
questions.why: Decides whether deriveSourceDefinition and the Fallow gate are deleted or kept as the fallback.
options: Delete it; no profile means map paths only and audit off
